newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - RED WINGS BEAT AVALANCHE, GO TO STANLEY CUP FINALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - RED WINGS BEAT AVALANCHE, GO TO STANLEY CUP FINALS.

text.p: The Detroit Red Wings advanced to the Stanley Cup Finals for the second time in three years, dethroning the champion Colorado Avalanche with a 3-1 victory Monday in Game 6 of the Western Conference finals.
The Red Wings won the best-of-seven series 4-2 and will play the Flyers in the National Hockey League's championship series beginning Saturday at Philadelphia.

"That's what we been working for, striving for all season," said Mike Vernon, the Detroit regular-season backup who started all of the Red Wings' playoff games. In the Colorado series he stopped 100 of 110 shots.
"Now we're going to the show, the big one."
"Our guys showed up tonight," said Detroit coach Scottie Bowman. "We dominated the game and played as if we didn't want to go back to Denver."

"One of the big reasons we have been as successful a team as we have been is that we don't look for excuses," said Colorado coach Marc Crawford. "We try to find solutions. We couldn't here, the Red Wings were too good. The Red Wings found a way and we didn't."
Detroit, which had 42 shots on goal to Colorado's 16, thoroughly dominated the Avalanche for the first 55 minutes before Scott Young scored off a rebound to cut the margin to 2-1.
But Brendan Shanahan scored into an empty net with 30 seconds remaining to seal the victory.

Martin Lapointe and Sergei Fedorov had the other goals for the Red Wings, whose 42-year Stanley Cup drought is the longest in the NHL. Detroit reached the Cup Finals in 1995 but was swept in four games by the New Jersey Devils.
"They were hungrier than we were and they played a lot better as a team," said Colorado captain and centre Joe Sakic. "They were the better team."
The Red Wings, coming off a 6-0 loss in Denver in Game 5, outshot Colorado in the first period 14-3.
But Patrick Roy kept the Wings from scoring.

He stopped Viacheslav Fetisov's one-time blast from just inside the blue line 90 seconds into the contest. He also got a glove on Shanahan's wrister from the low slot with 8:30 to go and smothered Steve Yzerman's wrist shot with just under two minutes left.
The Avalanche finally got a quality scoring chance about 2 1/2 minutes into the second period, but Vernon turned aside Valeri Kamensky's wrister from the left faceoff circle.

Detroit finally solved Roy 3:29 into the second period when Lapointe hopped off the bench, took a pass from Igor Larionov and unloaded a slap shot from the top of the left circle that tipped into the net off the heel of Roy's glove.
Colorado had a chance for the tying goal when Yves Sarault broke in 2-on-1, but he hurried his centering pass and missed Rene Corbet.
Vernon, who allowed the Avalanche only three goals in three games at Detroit, made a glove save with 12:43 to go in the second period on a slap shot by Sandis Ozolinsh.
Roy kept it a one-goal game by stopping Lapointe's backhander with 5:32 remaining, but Colorado was outshot over the first two periods 30-8.

Detroit kept up the pressure early in the third period. Roy had to make stops on Darren McCarty and Yzerman before the Avalanche had their best chance at the tying tally. With 14:48 to play, Sarault got in a step ahead of the Red Wings defence but shot just wide of the left post.

About a minute later, Vyacheslav Kozlov drew two defenders as he went behind the net before threading a pass in front. Fedorov, who had missed the final 9 1/2 minutes of the first minute after a hard check by Aaron Miller, put home his own rebound for his third goal of the series and a 2-0 lead.
The Red Wings continued to press as Fedorov and Fetisov failed on a 2-on-none with 8:49 to play and Yzerman flubbed a backhander on a breakaway with 5:30 left.

The Avalanche got on the board with 5:12 remaining. Vernon stopped Adam Deadmarsh's shot from the left circle, but was helpless as Young scored his fourth playoff goal on the rebound. It came on Colorado's 15th shot of the game and ended the Avalanche's drought at Detroit at 140 minutes, one second.

Yzerman, who has spent his entire 14-year career with the Red Wings, nearly sealed the win with 3:40 to go, but Roy got a piece of his wrister from the bottom of the left circle and the puck caromed off the left post.
The Avalanche totalled eight shots in the third period and were outshot for the series 215-127.
The Avalanche, who entered the conference finals leading the league on the power play at 28.8 percent, went 0-for-3 in Game 6 and 2-for-28 in the series.
The Flyers eliminated the New York Rangers four games to one on Sunday in the Eastern Conference finals.
